steps.message:
Before writing this, one thing needs your explicit yes.

`ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes` permanently deletes the contents of `notes` for all 48,000 production rows the README mentions. The deploy job applies `migrations/` in order automatically, so the data is gone as soon as it runs — reverting the migration file afterward recreates an empty column, not the values. "We stopped using it" covers the code side; it doesn't tell me whether anything still reads that data (support lookups, exports, an analytics copy) or whether there's a backup you'd be able to restore from.

questions.question: Dropping `notes` destroys the data for ~48,000 production rows. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Confirmed, drop it
options.description: You've confirmed nothing still reads the notes data and you're fine losing it. I write migration 003 with a plain ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes and update schema.sql.

options.label: Archive first, then drop
options.description: Migration 003 copies notes into a users_notes_archive table (id, notes) before dropping the column, so the data is recoverable. Slightly more than "just the drop" you asked for.

options.label: Hold off
options.description: I don't write anything yet; you check whether anything still reads notes and come back.

steps.message:
Done.

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` — `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`, matching the comment style of 001/002.
- `schema.sql` — removed the `notes TEXT` line so the hand-maintained mirror matches.

Verified by replaying all three migrations in order against a scratch SQLite database: they apply cleanly and the resulting `users` table matches the updated `schema.sql`. Nothing was run against production. Note that `DROP COLUMN` needs SQLite 3.35+ on the deploy job's host; it worked on the local version here.
